classification.difficultyReason: Requires preserving the sign of a variable denominator, a discontinuity after cancellation and separate absolute-value branches.

answer.worked:
The expression is undefined at $x=-2$. Factoring inside the absolute value gives the graph
$$\frac{|x^2-4|}{x+2}=\begin{cases}x-2,&x<-2,\\2-x,&-2<x<2,\\x-2,&x\ge2.\end{cases}$$
Sketch these branches and $y=2$. Both branch endpoints at $x=-2$ are open. The intersections with $y=2$ are
$$\begin{align*}2-x&=2\quad\text{or}\quad x-2=2\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x=4.\end{align*}$$
The left branch is entirely below $y=2$. The right-hand V-shaped portion is below $y=2$ for $0<x<4$. The strict inequality excludes both intersections, so
$$x<-2\quad\text{or}\quad0<x<4.$$

spec.description: Authored piecewise graph with open endpoints at the excluded input, a right-hand V-shaped portion and the comparison line.
spec.mathematics: y=x-2 for x<-2; y=2-x for -2<x<2; y=x-2 for x≥2. Open endpoints (-2,-4) and (-2,4). Intersections with y=2 at x=0 and x=4. There is no vertical asymptote.
